transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um... I guess... I just can't really shake this feeling lately. Like... like I've ruined things for everyone. I've been falling behind at work, and... the apartment situation is just kind of losing control. I don't know. I just feel like I deserve whatever bad thing happens next. So... yeah. That's why I'm here.
Have you noticed yourself losing interest in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or activities?

Yeah, I guess. Um... most days I just wake up with this... I don't know, this flat, heavy feeling. Sadness, I suppose. 

The things that usually kind of reset me... like putting on a record, or tinkering with electronics... they just don't really reach me right now. So... yeah.
Do you find yourself feeling guilty or responsible for things that you don’t have control over, or feeling like you’re a bad person even when you haven’t done anything wrong?

I mean... yeah. That's kind of what I was trying to say before. I just can't really shake it. 

Letting myself fall so far behind at work, and... the apartment getting completely out of control. It's all on me. I just feel like I've ruined things for everyone. So... yeah. I feel like I deserve whatever bad stuff happens next. I don't really know what else to say about it.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or on the flip side, feeling restless or fidgety lately?

I mean... maybe a little slower. Like... at work, sometimes my hands just kind of hover over the keyboard. It takes me a lot longer to get through simple support tickets. I don't know, it's just... it's almost like my brain and body are running on a delayed connection or something. But... yeah. That's about it.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight lately—like eating a lot more or less than usual?
Not really, no. Um... I guess I'm eating about the same. I haven't really paid attention to my weight or anything, but... no, I don't think anything's changed there.
Have you had any thoughts about hurting yourself or would you be better off dead?

I mean... I wouldn't actually do anything to hurt myself. I don't have a plan or anything like that. But... sometimes I just think it would be easier if I didn't wake up. Then nobody would have to deal with me anymore. But... yeah, I wouldn't actually do anything.
How long have you been feeling this way?

Um... I guess it's been about a year and two months. Give or take. It kind of started after a pipe burst at my old place. I had to move into a smaller apartment and... I don't know, my routines just sort of fell apart after that. So... yeah. About that long.
Have you ever felt this way before, or experienced a similar episode of depression in the past?
Um... no. Not really. I don't think I've ever felt like this before. Just... since the move, I guess.
Would you say that your movements or reactions have become noticeably slower to others, like people have mentioned you seem to be moving through molasses or taking longer to respond?

I don't really know if other people have noticed. I haven't asked. But... at work, I guess. Sometimes my hands just... hover over the keyboard. It takes me a lot longer to answer simple support tickets now. It just feels like... I don't know, like my brain and my body are running on a delayed connection or something. So... yeah. I guess so.
Have you ever thought about how you might hurt yourself, even if you don’t have a plan or intend to act on it?

Um... no. Not really. I don't... I don't have a plan or anything like that. I just... sometimes I think it would be easier if I just... didn't wake up. Then nobody would have to deal with me anymore. But I wouldn't actually do anything.
Would you say that your movements or speech have slowed down so much that other people might notice, like you’re moving in slow motion or taking much longer to respond to questions?
Um... I think I just mentioned that. With the... the keyboard thing at work. It just takes me longer to get through the tickets now. So... yeah. Like I said.
Have you ever experienced periods where you felt unusually energized, needed less sleep, or had racing thoughts, even if it felt good at the time?
No. I... I've never felt like that. I'm just tired all the time.
Have you ever had a period of time before this one where you felt down, lost interest in things, or experienced similar struggles, even if it was less severe?
No. Um... I don't think so. Just... just recently, I guess. Nothing before this.
Have you ever had a time before this where you felt down, lost interest in things, or experienced similar struggles, even if it wasn’t as bad as it is now?
I... didn't you just ask me that? Um... no. Like I said, it's just been recently. I haven't had this before.
Have you ever had a period lasting two weeks or more where you felt down or lost interest in things before this current time?
No. I... I don't really know why you keep asking me that. It's still no. Just... just this current time. I haven't had this happen before.
Have you ever had a time in your life before this one where you felt down most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks?
Look... the answer is still no. I've never felt like this before now. I don't know what else you want me to say.
Have you ever had any shorter periods, even just a few days, where you felt down or lost interest in things before this current episode started?
No. Not for a few days either. It's just... never happened before.
Have you ever had any short periods, even just a few days, where you felt down or lost interest in things before this current episode started?
I... didn't you just ask me that? It's still no. I really don't have anything else to tell you about it.

inference_history.note: The patient endorsed persistent sadness and anhedonia, which are key features of major depressive disorder and persistent depressive disorder. This makes stress-related disorders like F43.22 less likely, so it has been removed from the candidate list.

This turn ruled out significant changes in appetite or weight (excluding F32.0 and F33.0) and self-harm intent with no active plan (reducing likelihood of F32.3 and F33.3, but not fully ruling them out). Psychomotor slowing and persistent guilt remain prominent.

The duration of symptoms being approximately 14 months supports the diagnosis of persistent depressive disorder (dysthymia) as well as the possibility of a single or recurrent moderate to severe depressive episode. Psychomotor slowing and guilt are prominent features, but there is no history of prior episodes or current psychotic features. The lack of significant changes in appetite or weight slightly favors moderate presentations.
